seed: Objects of type `player` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [target] show mixed outcomes: gone x1, x x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Two mirror axes on a 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks: H = wall block row, V = wall block column. ACTION5 cycles selection H -> V -> pieces (sorted by min block). A1/A2 move H or the selected piece by one block row; A3/A4 move V or the selected piece by one block column.
Reflections: pieces mirror across V as visible gray reflections. Mirrors across H and across both axes are invisible occluders (solid -1 ring, transparent centre). No reflection is drawn on blocks a piece occupies.
Rendering: per-block sprite stacks (piece > visible reflection > invisible reflection > target > wall); a block centre shows the first solid sprite, otherwise the topmost sprite's fill. The frame is then re-extracted: walls and players are 4-connected components of their own cells plus all 0 cells, ranked by bbox (x,y); targets merge while bbox gap <= 4.
Hypothesis result: the player gone-vs-x outcome under A1 next to targets is just renaming. Piece ranks count the visible wall 0-dots, and that count changes as H mo
